name: TGS ASA
reason: Seismic data and acquisition business whose earnings track oil & gas exploration capex: reporting-currency (USD) EPS swung from 1.43 (2019) to -1.63 (2020) and is now 0.09 (0.06x its 10y max) with 10y avg ROIC of 2.5%.

name: Europris ASA
reason: Cheap-but-ordinary Norwegian discount retailer: NOK EPS 5.09 is still below the 2021 Covid peak of 6.58 (5y CAGR 1.0%) and EBIT margin is at the 9th pctile (8.0% vs 11.0% avg) as the Swedish OoB acquisition dilutes returns; no moat that makes it special.

name: SSP Group PLC
reason: Travel food-and-beverage concessionaire on airport/rail contracts: GBP adjusted EPS 0.11 is under half the 2019 level of 0.24 after the pandemic, shares grew 4.2%/yr, net debt/EBITDA is 2.65x and adjusted vs GAAP gap averages 329%.

name: Allwyn AG
reason: History is OPAP's Greek lottery/betting record (EUR EPS 0.47 to 1.28, 33% EBIT margin) but the 2025-26 combination into Allwyn transforms the group, consensus FY1 is -29.1%, earnings rest on state-granted lottery licences and the KKCG controlling shareholder adds governance risk.

name: IntegraFin Holdings PLC
reason: Transact adviser platform has a sticky franchise but revenue is tiered fees on assets under administration, so earnings track market levels (capital-markets lens, as MORN/AMP in the US run); GBP EPS grew only 0.11 to 0.17 over 2018-25 (~6%/yr) and FactSet EBIT margin is distorted by policyholder items.

name: Sunrise Communications AG
reason: Swiss telecom spun out of Liberty Global in 2024 with CHF GAAP EPS losses every year (-3.05/-5.07/-1.56), EBIT margin ~1% and net debt/EBITDA of 4.84x; a leveraged, low-growth regulated-competitive market with no route to 7% EPS growth.

name: METRO AG
reason: Cash-and-carry wholesaler with shrinking revenue (10y CAGR -1.4%), EUR EPS negative in 4 of the last 5 years, FactSet EBIT margin below zero throughout and net debt/EBITDA of 7.68x; fails the balance-sheet and earnings-quality tests.

name: Atea ASA
reason: Low-margin Nordic IT hardware/software reseller (3.7% EBIT margin, at its 10y high) with NOK EPS of 7.50 in 2021 and 7.84 in 2025 (~1%/yr since) and heavy public-sector tender exposure; cheap-but-ordinary with no moat that makes it special.

name: DOF Group ASA
reason: Offshore vessel owner and subsea contractor whose day rates follow the oil & gas cycle; USD EBIT margin 29.1% is at the top of its short post-restructuring record (100th pctile) and consensus FY3 is -3.6%.

name: Amplifon SpA
reason: Global hearing-care retail leader with a demographic tailwind, but EUR adjusted EPS fell from 0.98 (2022) to 0.68 (2025), EBIT margin is at the 9th pctile (8.8% vs 11.5% avg), acquisitions consumed 0.8x 10y FCF and OTC/consumer-earbud hearing aids are a credible 5-yr threat to the store model.

name: Imperial Brands PLC
reason: Structurally declining cigarette volumes: GBP adjusted EPS grew only 4.0%/yr over 10 years with 2 of 10 years >=7%, so the 7% route depends on buybacks and pricing, and next-generation products and regulation threaten the base; a cash cow without growth.

name: Vicat SA
reason: Cement producer with commodity-like pricing and 10y avg ROIC of only 5.0%; EUR EPS 6.09 is 0.99x its 10y max with EBIT margin at its 10y high (12.0% vs 9.5% avg, 100th pctile), so earnings sit at a cyclical peak.

name: Technip Energies NV
reason: Net-cash LNG/downstream engineering contractor with EUR EPS growth of 12%/yr since 2020, but earnings depend on lumpy EPC awards tied to energy capex and fixed-price project execution (consensus FY1 -10.9% then +61%), so 5-10 yr earnings cannot be forecast with confidence.

name: Edenred SA
reason: High-quality benefits/mobility network (ROIC ~54%, EUR EPS 0.85 to 2.59, 7/10 years >=7%) but Brazil's PAT meal-voucher fee caps and French titre-restaurant reform are live regulatory threats (consensus FY1 -19.4%) and float income depends on interest rates.

name: Husqvarna AB
reason: Weather- and consumer-cyclical outdoor power equipment maker: SEK adjusted EPS 3.14 is 0.41x its 2021 peak, 10y EPS CAGR is -0.9% and EBIT margin is at the 9th pctile; no forecastable route to 7% growth.

name: Bunzl plc
reason: Consumables distributor whose growth has been bought (acquisitions 0.5x 10y FCF) while organic growth stalled: GBP EPS fell from 1.90 (2023) to 1.82 (2025) and consensus FY2-FY3 is only 4.9%/4.6%, below the 7% bar.

name: Trigano SA
reason: Motorhome/caravan maker in a consumer-durable cycle: EUR EPS ran from 7.21 (2020) to a 19.42 peak (2024) and fell 35% to 12.59 in 2025 as post-Covid demand normalised; earnings follow leisure-vehicle demand, not a forecastable driver.

name: AFRY AB
reason: Acquisition-built Nordic engineering consultancy (acquisitions 0.66x 10y FCF, shares +2.3%/yr) with SEK EPS 10.44 below the 2019 level of 12.37, EBIT margin at the 18th pctile and AI threat to labour-based billing.

name: Moltiply Group S.p.A.
reason: Italian mortgage/insurance broker and comparison sites with EUR EPS up 0.53 to 1.63 over 10 years, but mortgage volumes follow the rate/housing cycle, acquisitions exceed 10y FCF (1.15x) and adjusted EPS runs 84% above GAAP on average.

name: Mercedes-Benz Group AG
reason: Premium carmaker with cyclical, China- and EV-exposed earnings: EUR EPS fell from 13.55 (2022) to 5.34 (2025), 10y EPS CAGR -2.4% and EBIT margin at the 27th pctile; tariff and EV-transition threats rule out a confident forecast.
